$comment: The source of sf-chart-metric 1.0.0 (standard simai.smart-component 1.3.14 in the 1.4 form, vocabulary 1.1.5): the dated alias of SIMAI Framework's sf-tile-metric until 2027-01-01. Decision C168 made sf-tile-metric (ui-source src/smart/tile-metric, a free Smart component) the Framework's metric tile, with a chart slot that takes sf-chart-sparkline; this element, the set's tile of 0.1.x (docs/DECISIONS.md D1, D19), is retired into it as sf-message-log was into sf-list-feed (ui-source 2874cb5d, journal record tag-sf-message-log-to-sf-list-feed): a subclass of the class that defines sf-tile-metric, the former names mapped, no code of its own.

label.summary: What the number is, in a few words: the tile's accessible name. sf-tile-metric's label: without it the tile is named «Показатель».

value.summary: The number. Unset, the tile says «—». sf-tile-metric's value.

format.summary: sf-tile-metric's format: number, integer, decimal-<n>, percent (a share 0..1), compact, currency-<CODE> or unit-<Intl unit>, in the page's language; money is whole unless a precision word is given (currency-RUB decimal-2). The change and the limit are written the same way.

previous.summary: The value of the previous period; the change is worked out from it when delta is not given. The same setting of sf-tile-metric.

delta.summary: The change itself, when the page has it; it wins over previous. The same setting of sf-tile-metric.

delta-format.summary: How the change is written: its share of the previous value, the difference in the value's format, or both. Without a previous value it is the difference. The same setting of sf-tile-metric.

period-text.summary: What the change is against, after it: «к прошлой неделе». The same setting of sf-tile-metric.

better.summary: Whether a rise is good: up for sales, down for server load or errors, none when neither. The change's tone follows its meaning, not its sign. The same setting of sf-tile-metric.

max.summary: A limit: the tile shows «value of max» with a meter (storage, a licence, a quota). The same setting of sf-tile-metric.

limit-text.summary: The words under the meter instead of «45 ГБ из 100 ГБ». The same setting of sf-tile-metric.

status.summary: The page's statement about the number, in the shared status vocabulary: sf-tile-metric's status, a status icon of that tone before the hint. Thresholds are the page's (sf-tile-metric's warning-at and error-at).

hint.summary: A short line beside the status. The same setting of sf-tile-metric.

href.summary: Makes the whole tile one link to this address. The same setting of sf-tile-metric.

openable.summary: Without href: makes the whole tile one button that sends open. The same setting of sf-tile-metric.

size.summary: The rung of the size ladder: the value's text, the gaps. 1/2 for a dense row, 2 for a page's headline figure. The same setting of sf-tile-metric.

data-state.summary: The former state setting, kept until 2027-01-01: loading is sf-tile-metric's loading (the label stays, each waiting line keeps its place, aria-busy); empty draws the tile without its value («—»); auto and ready follow the value. Write loading on sf-tile-metric instead.

open.summary: A person pressed an openable tile (a click, Enter or Space): sf-tile-metric's open {id}, sent as sf-tile-metric-open and, until 2027-01-01, as sf-chart-metric-open with the same detail; the host opens the details.

chart.$comment: sf-tile-metric's chart slot: a child with slot="chart", as a rule an sf-chart-sparkline of the same series, laid across the tile's width, 32 high, in the hint's colour; the tile keeps the live node.

skeleton.$comment: The value arrives after the first paint when the host loads it: data-state loading is sf-tile-metric's loading, which holds the tile's size with a skeleton of each waiting line (standard 1.3.8 §5.4).

accessibility.x-keys: sf-tile-metric's: a plain tile is a group named by its label and takes no focus. With href it is one link, with openable one native button: a single Tab stop, Enter (and Space for the button) opens. The change says its direction in words beside the arrow, the limit is a meter with its value text, the status says its word beside the icon.

aliases.$comment: Dated aliases of sf-chart-metric for the shim (core/js/aliases.js, standard §16 item 20), installed on the element by the Smart base. Since 1.0.0 the element is sf-tile-metric's heir: the tile sends sf-tile-metric-open {id}, and the former name follows with the same, larger detail (0.1.x sent {}).

rows.note: the element is sf-tile-metric's heir; the tile sends sf-tile-metric-open {id} and the former name follows with that detail

x-summary: The dated alias of SIMAI Framework's metric tile sf-tile-metric until 2027-01-01 (decision C168): the same settings, the chart slot for an sf-chart-sparkline, the former data-state, event name and public variables mapped onto the tile. Write <sf-tile-metric> for new pages.
x-decisions: 1.0.0 (2026-11-17, decision C168, the SIMAI Framework dispatcher's task K-10; docs/DECISIONS.md D19): a major. sf-chart-metric is retired into SIMAI Framework's sf-tile-metric, which took over its settings by name (sf-tile-metric x-decisions: «the settings keep sf-chart-metric 0.1.0's names») and is the Framework's metric tile with a chart slot that takes sf-chart-sparkline. The element is now the tile's dated alias until 2027-01-01, made as sf-message-log 2.0.0 was made sf-list-feed's (ui-source 2874cb5d, ui-pro components/src/smart/message-log): a subclass of the class that defines sf-tile-metric, so it draws the tile's markup (.sf-tile-metric, .sf-tile-metric-*) with the tile's sheet; the bundle carries none of the tile's code. No new feature lands here.

tag: the alias row {from: sf-chart-metric, to: sf-tile-metric, since 2026-11-17, remove_after 2027-01-01} is given at runtime once the element is defined (core tag-aliases.js registerTagAliasRows), so canonicalTag, tagSelector and isTag know it; the first <sf-chart-metric> a page connects is noted in SF.deprecations and once on the console. The row is given after the definition, not before: given first, the Smart base would define a bare subclass when the tile is defined and the former names below would be lost. SIMAI Framework's static tag table does not carry the row while the set defines the element.

settings: label, value, format, previous, delta, delta-format, period-text, better, max, limit-text, status, hint, href, openable and size are the tile's own, unchanged in name and meaning; the tile's newer settings (value-text, unit, warning-at, error-at, loading) work on the alias too. data-state, which the tile does not have, is mapped: loading is the tile's loading, empty draws no value. What the tile draws differently is the tile's: money is whole by default (C168 (2)), the change is a tonal badge, the status an icon with its word.
events: open is the tile's open {id} (vocabulary 1.1.5 §5); sf-tile-metric-open is sent and the former name sf-chart-metric-open follows with that detail (aliases, mode detail-adds: 0.1.x sent {}).

css-variables: --sf-chart-metric-background-color, -value-color and -hover-background-color feed the tile's --sf-tile-metric-background-color, -value-color and -hover-background-color on the tile inside the alias, a page's own tile variables still reaching it when the former ones are unset; --sf-chart-metric-min-inline-size is the alias host's narrowest width. The tile has no counterpart for -label-color, -positive-color, -negative-color and -meter-color (the change takes the status tone of its badge, the meter the status's): they are no longer read.
relations: cl-tile-metric only. The tile brings its own (sf-progress-bar, sf-badge, sf-icon, sr-only); the chart core is not needed, because nothing of a chart is drawn here.
0.1.x history: 0.1.0 (2026-11-02) the set's metric tile, the catalogue's KPI and Larena's metric tile (D1); 0.1.1 (2026-11-09) took the shared chart core from the runtime (D18).

ai_guidance.use_when: Do not use sf-chart-metric in new markup: it is the dated alias of SIMAI Framework's sf-tile-metric until 2027-01-01. Write <sf-tile-metric> with an sf-chart-sparkline in slot="chart".
do_not: Do not write sf-chart-metric in new pages; write sf-tile-metric
Do not listen for sf-chart-metric-open in new code; listen for sf-tile-metric-open
Do not infer a status from the value; give warning-at and error-at, or status with a hint
ai_guidance.minimal_example: <sf-tile-metric label="Выручка за неделю" value="1250000" previous="1100000" format="currency-RUB"><sf-chart-sparkline slot="chart" label="Выручка по дням"></sf-chart-sparkline></sf-tile-metric>

accessibility.focus: None for a plain tile; one Tab stop for a link or a button tile.

$comment: sf-chart-metric is a dated alias of SIMAI Framework's sf-tile-metric: the element is a subclass of the class that defines sf-tile-metric, so the tile's rule (its code, its sheet, its own relations: sf-progress-bar, sf-badge, sf-icon, sr-only) comes with it. This rule's sheet keeps only the host and the former public variables feeding the tile's.
